svg.text: The adolescent in hospital is not a large child
What they need most is privacy, honesty and some control
Consultation that works
Offer part of the visit without the parent
Explain confidentiality and its limits at the start,
before she tells you anything
Ask her, not her mother, how she is
Speak to the condition, not the behaviour
Curtains are not privacy if voices carry
Why adolescents stop taking medicines
The tablets are the reminder of being different
Boarding school: nowhere private to take them
Side effects that show, such as weight or skin
Feeling well, so the illness seems finished
Fear of a friend seeing and asking why
None of these is solved by repeating the instructions
Asking about adherence without producing a polite lie
Not: “You are taking your medicines, aren’t you?” — that question has only one answer
Instead: “Most people miss doses sometimes. Which days did you miss last week?”
Normalise it, then ask her to name the days. Then ask what got in the way.
Transition to adult services
Prepare it over years, not at the last appointment: let her book, ask and answer herself
Handing over notes is not a transition; the young person is what has to be handed over
Disengagement after transfer is common, and it is where these patients are lost
